subject: Mental Models
title: Marginal Thinking
description: A fast breakdown of Marginal Thinking for builders.

hook.text: A factory already built ten thousand widgets.

buildup.text: Marginal thinking ignores past costs and focuses on the next unit. What does one more cost and what does one more earn?

discovery.text: Airlines sell last-minute seats cheaply for this reason.

twist.text: People fail at marginal thinking daily. They consider the total price of a gym membership instead of the cost per visit.

climax.text: For any decision, ask: what changes if I do one more or one less? That marginal question cuts through noise fast.

punchline.text: Ignore the total. Focus on the next unit.

quiz.question: Why do airlines sell last-minute seats cheaply?
options: They want to attract poor travelers
The plane flies regardless, so any extra seat sold is nearly pure profit
